title: Performance vs Consistency: Evaluating a Foundation Model in Lung-RADS Screening
abstract: arXiv:2609.22281v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Foundation models have recently demonstrated strong capabilities across a wide range of medical imaging tasks. However, their performance in structured clinical interpretation settings remains insufficiently explored. In lung cancer screening, interpretative variability persists despite standardized frameworks such as Lung-RADS. In this study, we evaluate MedGemma, a medical general-purpose foundation model derived from Gemini and its fine-tuned version adapted for lung cancer detection and diagnosis, compared against radiologists performing Lung-RADS v2022 assessment on the NLST dataset. Twelve radiologists independently evaluated each case in a multi-reader design, enabling quantification of inter-reader variability. Radiologists achieved a mean AUC of 0.90, with substantial variability across readers (range: 0.80-0.94). The native foundation model achieved an AUC of 0.70, failing to reach clinically relevant performance. In contrast

translated_title: 性能与一致性：评估基础模型在Lung-RADS肺癌筛查中的表现
translated_abstract: 基础模型近来在广泛的医学影像任务中展现出强大的能力。然而，它们在结构化临床解读场景中的表现仍未得到充分探索。在肺癌筛查中，尽管存在Lung-RADS这样的标准化框架，解读结果的可变性依然存在。在本研究中，我们评估了MedGemma——一个由Gemini衍生的医疗通用基础模型——及其针对肺癌检测与诊断微调后的版本，并将其与在NLST数据集上进行Lung-RADS v2022评估的放射科医生进行比较。十二名放射科医生在多读者设计中独立评估每个病例，从而能够量化读者间差异。放射科医生的平均AUC为0.90，但读者之间存在较大差异（范围：0.80-0.94）。原生基础模型的AUC为0.70，未能达到临床相关性能。相比之下……
tldr: 本研究在NLST数据集上以多读者设计将MedGemma基础模型及其微调版本与十二名放射科医生的Lung-RADS v2022评估进行对比，发现放射科医生平均AUC达0.90但读者间差异显著，而原生基础模型AUC仅0.70，未达到临床相关性能。
en_tdlr: Using a multi-reader design on the NLST dataset, this study benchmarks MedGemma and its fine-tuned version against twelve radiologists performing Lung-RADS v2022 assessment, finding that radiologists achieve a mean AUC of 0.90 with substantial inter-reader variability, while the native foundation model reaches only 0.70, failing to attain clinically relevant performance.
